fields.h1: Build a Cookie Exchange Sign-Up Sheet That Plans the Swap
fields.hero_description: Build a cookie exchange sign up sheet that takes each cookie off the list once claimed and tells every baker how many to bake.
fields.features_heading: What the Sheet Settles Before Baking Day
fields.features_subheading: A paper sheet holds names and cookies. This one also blocks repeats, does the dozen math, and keeps allergy details with each batch.
fields.feature_1:
A cookie list that never repeats

List the cookies you want on the table, or let bakers name their own. Once someone claims a cookie, it leaves the list, and the next baker picks from what is still open.
fields.feature_2:
Dozens worked out from the head count

Set a rule such as 6 cookies for each participant. The app multiplies it by the number of sign-ups and tells each baker how many dozen to bring once the list is full.
fields.feature_3:
Allergy details stored with each batch

Each baker ticks what their batch contains, such as peanuts, tree nuts, or wheat. The host gets an email listing every batch with peanuts before the tables are set up.
fields.feature_4:
Recipes collected on the same form

Ask for the recipe along with the cookie name. Every recipe lands in one place, so the host can hand out a full set on swap day without chasing anyone by text message.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders that say what to bring

The app emails each baker the week before with their cookie, their dozen count, and the drop-off time. A baker who has not confirmed gets a second email two days out.
fields.feature_6:
Sign-ups kept in a database you own

Every baker, cookie, and recipe stays in a database you own, ready for next December's swap. On paid plans, export the full code of the sheet to your GitHub repository.

plan.angle: Searchers for cookie exchange sign up sheet find printable grids with a name column and a cookie column, and the host still has to spot duplicate recipes, work out how many dozen each baker owes, and chase allergy notes by text. This page shows the sheet doing that work in four real swaps: an office swap where a claimed cookie leaves the list, a street swap where the baking count follows the head count, a scout troop swap that flags peanut batches for their own table, and a book club swap by mail that gives each member one address to ship to.
tab_stories: At Nimbleton Insurance, Sigrun Wenstrom lists 14 cookie types for the office swap, and once a coworker claims snickerdoodles they leave the list, so Wilhelmus Brunvoll sees only the 9 still open.
Brynja Asplund caps the Cardwyn Lane swap at 12 households and asks for 6 cookies per participant, and when the 12th household signs up every baker gets an email saying to bake 6 dozen.
Troop 418 leader Elske Eskeland asks each family which allergens their batch contains, and when 3 of 18 batches list peanuts she gets an email naming them so they go on a separate table.
Ida Pettigrove runs the Pettigrove Book Club swap by mail, and once all 16 members sign up each one gets an email with one other member's mailing address and a December 8 ship-by date.
